G1500.def:
εἰκῇ (-ῆ, Rec., as in cl.), adv., 
[in LXX: Proverbes 28:25 (εἰκῇ)* ;] 
__1. without cause or reason: Matthieu 5:22 (E, mg.), Colossiens 2:18 (ICC). 
__2. vainly, fruitlessly, to no purpose: Romains 13:4, 1 Corinthiens 15:2, Galates 3:4 4:11, Colossiens 2:18.
†

G1501.def:
εἴκοσι (never -ιν in WH, cf. Bl., §5, 3, and note), indecl., οἱ, αἱ, τά, 
twenty: Luc 14:31, Jean 6:19, Actes 1:15 27:28, 1 Corinthiens 10:8, Apocalypse 4:4, 10 5:8 11:16 19:4.†

G1502.def:
εἴκω, 
[in LXX: 2 Rois 12:7 (ענה), Wis.18:25, 4Ma.1:6 * ;] 
to yield: Galates 2:5 (cf. ὑπ-είκω).†

G1503.def: εἴκω (obsolete pres.), see: ἔοικα Transcriber note: This form does not occur in Abbott-Smith. It should be on p. 158..

G1504.def:
εἰκών, -όνος (cf. ἔοικα), 
[in LXX chiefly for צֶלֶם ;] 
an image, likeness: Matthieu 22:20, Marc 12:16, Luc 20:24, Romains 1:23, 1 Corinthiens 15:49, Apocalypse 13:14, 15 14:9, 11 15:2 16:2 19:20 20:4; opposite to σκιά, Hébreux 10:1; of man, εἰ. θεοῦ, 1 Co 11:7; of the regenerate, εἰ. τ. θεοῦ Colossiens 3:10 (see Lft., in l.); εἰ. τ. υἱοῦ τ. θεοῦ, Romains 8:29, 2 Corinthiens 3:18; of Christ, εἰ. τ. θεοῦ, 2 Corinthiens 4:4, Colossiens 1:15.† SYN.: ὁμοίωμα, denoting resemblance, which may however be merely accidental. εἰ. is a derived likeness and like the head on a coin or the parental likeness in a child, implies an archetype. Cf. also εἶδος, appearance, not necessarily based on reality; σκιά, a shadowed resemblance; χαρακτήρ, the impress of a stamp; μόρφη (which see), the form as indicative of the inner being.

G1505.def:
εἰλικρινία (Rec., cl., -κρινεία), -ας, ἡ 
(εἰλικρινής), [in LXX: Wis.7:25 A * ;] 
sincerity, purity: 1 Corinthiens 5:8, 2 Corinthiens 1:12 2:17.†

G1514.def:
εἰρηνεύω 
(εἰρήνη), [in LXX chiefly for שׁלם, שׁקט ;] 
__1. to bring to peace, reconcile (so 1Ma.6:60). 
__2. to keep peace, be at peace: Marc 9:50, Romains 12:18, 2 Corinthiens 13:11, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:13 (cf. Sir.28:9; Cremer, 246).
†

G1515.def:
εἰρήνη, -ης, ἡ, 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁלוֹם ;] 
peace; 
__1. of public peace, freedom from war: Luc 14:32, Actes 12:20 24:2; of the church, Ac 9:31. 
__2. Of peace between persons, concord, agreement : Matthieu 10:34, Luc 12:51, Romains 14:17, 1 Corinthiens 7:15, Galates 5:22, Jacques 3:18; ζητεῖν εἰ., 1 Pierre 3:11; διώκειν, 2 Timothée 2:22; ib. before μετὰ πάντων, Hébreux 12:14; by meton., of him who brings peace, Éphésiens 2:14. 
__3. As in LXX (= Heb. שָׁלוֹם, Aram. שְׁלָם), of a state of security and safety: Jean 16:33, Romains 2:10, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:3,́ whence the formulae, ὕπαγε (πορεύου) εἰς εἰ, Marc 5:34, Luc 7:50 (cf. 1 Rois 1:17, al.; לְכִי לְשָׁלוֹם); εἰ. ὑμῖν (שָׁלוֹם לָכֶם), Jean 20:19, 21, 26; ἀπολύειν ἐν εἰ., Luc 2:29, cf. 1 Corinthiens 16:11; ἡ εἰ. ὑμῶν, Matthieu 10:13, Luc 10:6; υἱὸς εἰρήνης, ib. 
__4. Of spiritual peace, the peace of Christ's kingdom (DCG, ii, 330f.): Luc 1:79 2:14 Jean 16:33, Romains 2:10 5:1 8:6, al.; ὁ κύριος τῆς εἰ., 2 Thessaloniciens 3:16; ὁ θεὸς τῆς εἰ., Romains 15:33 16:20, 2 Corinthiens 13:11, al.; in epistolary salutations, Romains 1:7, 1 Corinthiens 1:3, Galates 1:3, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:1, 1 Pierre 1:2, 2Jo.3, Apocalypse 1:4, al. (see Cremer, 244).

G1516.def:
είρηνικός, -ή, -όν
(εἰρήνη), [in LXX for שָׁלוֹם and cognates ;] 
peaceful: Hébreux 12:11, Jacques 3:17.†

G1517.def:
εἰρηνο-ποιέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Proverbes 10:10 * ;] 
to make peace: Colossiens 1:20.†

G1521.def:
εἰσ-άγω 
[in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא, hi. ;] 
to bring in: with accusative, Luc 2:27, Jean 18:16, Actes 7:45; before εἰς, Luc 22:54, Actes 9:8 21:28-29, 37 22:24, Hébreux 1:6; ὧδε, Luc 14:21.†

G1522.def:
είσ-ακούω 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁמַע, also for עָנָה, etc. ;] 
to listen to, in two senses; 
__(a) to obey: 1 Corinthiens 14:21 (cf. Deutéronome 1:43, Sir.3:6) 
__(b) to listen, assent to; pass., to be heard: of persons praying, Matthieu 6:7, Hébreux 5:7; of the prayer offered, Luc 1:13, Actes 10:31 (cf. Psaumes 4:2, Sir.34:26); see Cremer, 624).†

G1523.def:
εἰσ-δέχομαι 
[in LXX for קָבַץ ;] 
to admit, receive: 2 Corinthiens 6:17 (LXX) (Cremer, 687).†

G1524.def:
εἴσ-ειμι 
[in LXX for בּוֹא ;] 
to go in, enter: before εἰς, Actes 3:3 21:26, Hébreux 9:6; πρὸς Ἰάκωβον, Actes 21:18.†

G1525.def:
εἰσ-έρχομαι, 
[in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא ;] 
to go in or into, enter: Matthieu 9:25, Luc 7:45, al.; before εἰς, Matthieu 10:12, Marc 2:1, al.; before διά (πύλης, θύρας, etc.), Matthieu 7:13, Jean 10:1, al.; ὑπὸ τ. στέγην, Matthieu 8:8; with adv.: ὅπου, Marc 14:14, Hébreux 6:20; ὧδε, Matthieu 22:12; ἔσω, Matthieu 26:58; before πρός, with accusative of person(s), Marc 15:43, Luc 1:28, Actes 10:3 11:3 16:40 17:2 28:8, Apocalypse 3:20; of demons taking possession, Marc 9:25, Luc 8:30 22:3, Jean 13:27; of food, Matthieu 15:11, Actes 11:8. Metaphorical, of thoughts, Luc 9:46; εἰς κόπον, Jean 4:38; εἰς πειρασμόν, Matthieu 26:41, Luc 22:40, 46; of hope as an anchor, Hébreux 6:19; βοαί, Jacques 5:4; πνεῦμα ζωῆς, Apocalypse 11:11; εἰς τ. κόσμον (cf. Wis.2:24 14:14, Jean 18:37), Romains 5:12, Hébreux 10:5; in counterparts of Jewish Aram. phrases relating to the theocracy (cf. Dalman, Words, 116ff.): εἰς τ. γάμους, Matthieu 25:10; εἰς τ. χάραν τ. κυρίου, Matthieu 25:21, 23; εἰς τ. ζωήν, Matthieu 18:8, 9 19:17, Marc 9:43, 45; εἰς τ. βασιλ. τ. οὐρανῶν, Matthieu 5:20 7:21, al. (see: βασιλεία); εἰς τ. κατάπαυσιν, Hébreux 3:11, 18 4:1ff.; εἰς τ. δόξαν, Luc 24:26; εἰσ. καὶ ἐξερχ., to go in and out (like Heb. בוֹא וְצֵאת, Deutéronome 28:6, etc.), of familiar intercourse, Actes 1:21; figuratively, of moral freedom, Jean 10:9 (cf. ἐπ-, παρ-, συν-εισέρχομαι).

G1528.def:
εἰσ-καλέω, -ῶ, 
to call in: mid., with accusative of person(s), Actes 10:23.†

G1529.def:
εἴσ-οδος, -ου, ὁ 
(ὁδός) [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא ;] 
__1. a means of entering, place of entrance: Hébreux 10:19, 2 Pierre 1:11 (cf. Westc., He., l.with; MM, Exp., xii; but see infr.). 
__2. a going in, entrance: Actes 13:24; with genitive loc., Hébreux 10:19 (Thayer, see word; but see supr.); before εἰς, 2 Pierre 1:11 (Mayor, in l.; Thayer; but see supr.); πρός, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:9 2:1.†

G1530.def:
εἰσ-πηδάω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Amos 5:19 (בּוֹא), Da TH Sus 1:26* ;] 
to spring in, rush in: Actes 14:14 (Rec.), Actes 16:29 (for exx. from π., see MM, Exp., xii).†

G1531.def:
εἰσ-πορεύομαι 
[in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא ;] 
to go into, enter: Luc 8:16 11:33 19:30; before εἰς, Marc 1:21 6:56 11:2, Luc 22:10, Actes 3:2; πρός, with accusative of person(s), Actes 28:30; ὅπου, Marc 5:40; κατά τ. οἴκους, house after house, Actes 8:3; of things (food), Matthieu 15:17, Marc 7:15, 18-19 Metaphorical (cf. εἰοέρχομαι, 2), Marc 4:19, Luc 18:24; εἰσ. καὶ ἐκπορ., to associate with, before μετά (cf. εἰσέρχομαι), Actes 9:28.†

G1532.def:
εἰσ-τρέχω 
[in LXX: 2Ma.5:26 * ;] 
to run in: Actes 12:14.†

G1533.def:
εἰσ-φέρω 
[in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא hi. ;] 
to bring in, into: with accusative of person(s), Luc 5:18-19; before εἰς, Matthieu 6:13, Luc 11:4; ἐπί, Luc 12:11; with accusative of thing(s), before εἰς, 1 Timothée 6:7; pass., Hébreux 13:11.†

G1534.def:
εἶτα 
adv., 
denoting sequence; 
__1. of time; then, next: Marc 8:25, Luc 8:12, Jean 13:5 19:27 20:27, 1 Timothée 3:10, Jacques 1:15; before genitive abs., Marc 4:17; in enumerations, 1 Corinthiens 15:5 15:7 15:24, 1 Timothée 2:13. 
__2. In argument; 
__(a) therefore, then, 
__(b) furthermore: Hébreux 12:9 (cf. εἶτεν).†

G1535.def:
εἴτε, see: εἰ.
εἰ, 
conjunctive particle, used in conditions and in indirect questions. 
__I. Conditional, if; 
__1. with indic, expressing a general assumption; 
__(a) pres.: before indic, pres., Matthieu 11:14, Romains 8:25, al.; before imperat., Marc 4:23 9:22, Jean 15:18, 1 Corinthiens 7:9, al.; before fut. indic., Luc 16:31, Romains 8:11, al.; before pf. or aor., with negation in apodosis, Matthieu 12:26, Romains 4:14, al.; similarly, before impf., Luc 17:6, Jean 8:39; before quæst., Matthieu 6:23, Jean 5:47 7:23 8:46, 1 Pierre 2:20; 
__(b) fut.: Matthieu 26:33, 1 Pierre 2:20; 
__(with) pf.: Jean 11:12, Romains 6:5, al.; 
__(d) aor.: Luc 16:11 19:8, Jean 13:32, 18:23, Apocalypse 20:15, al. 
__2. Where the assumption is certain = ἐπεί: Matthieu 12:28, Jean 7:4, Romains 5:17, al. 
__3. Of an unfulfilled condition, with indic, impf., aor. or plpf., before ἄν, with imp. or aor. (see: ἄν, I, i). 
__4. C. indic., after verbs denoting wonder, etc., sometimes, but not always, coupled with an element of doubt: Marc 15:44, 1 Jean 3:13, al. 
__5. C. indic., as in LXX (Nombres 14:3o, 1 Rois 14:45, al. = Heb. אִם), in oaths, with the formula of imprecation understood in a suppressed apodosis (WM, 627; Burton, §272): Marc 8:12, Hébreux 3:11" (LXX) 4:3 (LXX). 
__6. Rarely (cl.) with optative, to express a merely possible condition: Actes 24:19 27:39, 1 Corinthiens 14:10 15:37, I Pe3:14, 17. 
__II. Interrogative, if, whether. 
__1. As in cl., in indir. questions after verbs of seeing, asking, knowing, saying, etc.: with indic. pres., Matthieu 26:63, Marc 15:36, Actes 19:2, 2 Corinthiens 13:5, al.; fut., Marc 3:2, Actes 8:22, al.; aor., Marc 15:44, 1 Corinthiens 1:16, al.; with subjc. aor. (M, Pr., 194), Philippiens 3:12. 
__2. As in LXX (= Heb. אִם and interrog. הֲ, Genèse 17:17, al.; see WM, 639f.; Viteau, i, 22), in direct questions: Marc 8:23 (Tr., WH, txt.), Luc 13:23, 22:49, Actes 19:2, al.
__III. With other particles. 
__1. εἰ ἄρα, εἴγε, εἰ δὲ μήγε, see: ἄρα, γε. 
__2. εἰ δὲ καί, but if also: Luc 11:18; but even if, 1 Corinthiens 4:7, 2 Corinthiens 4:3 11:16. 
__3. εἰ δὲ μή, but if not, but if otherwise: Marc 2:21, 22 Jean 14:2, Apocalypse 2:5, al. 
__4. εἰ καί, if even, if also, although: Marc 14:29, Luc 11:8, 1 Corinthiens 7:21, 2 Corinthiens 4:16, Philippiens 2:17, al. 
__5. καὶ εἰ, even if, see: καί 
__6. εἰ μή, if not, unless, except, but only: Matthieu 24:22, Marc 2:26 6:5, Jean 9:33, 1 Corinthiens 7:17 (only), Galates 1:19 (cf. ἐὰν μή, 2:16; see Hort., Ja., xvi); ἐκτὸς εἰ μή, pleonastic (Bl., §65, 6), 1 Corinthiens 14:5 15:2, 1 Timothée 5:19. 
__7. εἰ μήν = cl. ἦ μήν (M, Pr., 46), in oaths, surely (Eze.33:27, al.): Hébreux 6:14. 
__8. εἴ πως, if haply: Actes 27:12, Romains 1:10. 
__9. εἴτε . . . εἴτε, whether . . . or; Romains 12:6-8, 1 Corinthiens 3:22 13:8, al.

G1537.def:
ἐκ (ἐξ), 
prep. with genitive, 
from out of, from (see Addendum, p. 492).
This entry is included here, but in the print version the entry is found on p. 492. ἐκ, before a vowel ἐξ, 
prep. with genitive, 
of motion outwards, separation from (opposite to εἰς; = Lat. e, ex), from out of, from among, from. 
__I. Of Place, 
__1. of motion, out of, forth from, off from: Jean 6:31, Actes 9:3, Galates 1:8, al.; esp. after verbs of motion, Matthieu 8:28 17:9, Marc 1:25 7:28, Jean 1:33 20:1, Actes 12:7, 17 27:30, al.; constr. praeg., σώζειν (διας) ἐκ, Ju 5, Actes 28:4. Metaphorical, Matthieu 7:4, 5, 1 Pierre 2:9; ἐκ τ. χειρός (-ῶν), before genitive of person(s), Luc 1:74, Jean 10:28, 29, 39, Actes 12:4 24:7, Apocalypse 19:2; πίνειν (which see) ἐκ; of the place from which an action proceeds, Luc 5:3 (cf. 12:36, Jean 13:4, 2 Corinthiens 2:4). 
__2. Of change from one place or condition to another: Jean 8:42, Romains 6:13 13:11, Apocalypse 7:14, al.; with ellips. of verb of motion, 2 Timothée 2:26, 2 Pierre 2:21, Apocalypse 2:21, al.
__3. Of separation or distinction from a number, before collective or pl. nouns: Matthieu 13:47, 49, Jean 12:1, Actes 3:15, 1 Pierre 1:3, al.; after εἷς, Matthieu 10:29 Luc 17:15, al.; οὐδείς, Jean 7:19, al.; πολλοί, Jean 11:19, al.; τις, Luc 11:15, al.; τίς, Matthieu 6:27, al.; in partitive phrase as subject of sentence, Jean 16:17; Hebraistically, ἐκ μέσου before genitive, = ἐκ (Heb. מִתּוֹךְ), Matthieu 13:49, al. 
__4. Of position or direction (so in cl. = ἔξω): ἐκ δεξιῶν (see: δεξιός); ἐξ ἐναντίας, Marc 15:39 (metaphorically, Tite 2:8); ἐκ ῥιζῶν (i.e., utterly), Matthieu 11:20. 
__II. Of Time, 
__1. of the point of time from which, from, since: ἐκ γενετῆς, Jean 9:1, cf. Marc 10:20, Luc 23:8, Actes 24:10, al. 
__2. Of succession in time: ἐκ δευτέρου, a second time, Marc 14:72, al., cf. Matthieu 26:44; ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας, from day to day, 2 Pierre 2:8. 
__III. Of Origin, 
__1. of nativity, lineage, race: κοίτην (ἐν γαστρί) ἔχειν, Romains 9:10, Matthieu 1:18; γεννᾶν ἐκ, Matthieu 1:3ff.; γεννᾶσθαι (γίνεσθαι) ἐκ, Jean 3:6 8:41, Galates 4:4; ἐκ πνεύματος (θεοῦ), Jean 1:13 3:5ff., al. ἔρχεσθαι, εἶναι, etc., ἐκ τ. πολέως, Jean 1:44; φυλῆς, Luc 2:36, al.; τ. ἐξουσίας Ἡρῴδου, Luc 23:7; ὁ ὢν ἐκ τ. γῆς, Jean 3:31. 
__2. Of the author, occasion or source: Matthieu 5:37, Jean 2:16, Romains 2:29, 1 Corinthiens 8:6, Galates 5:8, al.; ἐκ (τ. θεοῦ, 1 Corinthiens 7:7, 2 Corinthiens 5:1, 1 Jean 4:7; ἐκ τ. πατρός, Jean 6:65, al.; ἐκ τ. γῆς ἐστιν, λαλεῖ, Jean 3:31; εκ καρδίας, Romains 6:17, cf. Marc 12:30, 1 Timothée 1:5; ἐκ ψυχῆς, Éphésiens 6:6, Colossiens 3:23; ἐκ πίστεως, Romains 14:23; κρίνειν ἐκ, Luc 19:22, Apocalypse 20:12. 
__3. Of the agent, after passive verbs: Matthieu 15:5, Marc 7:11, 2 Corinthiens 2:2, al.; frequently in Re after αδικεῖσθαι (2:11), etc. 
__4. Of cause, dependence, source of supply: τ. πόνου (των), Apocalypse 16:10, 11; τ. φωνῶν, Apocalypse 8:13; ἐκ τούτου, Jean 6:66 19:12 (but see Meyer, in ll.); ἐκ θεοῦ λαλεῖν, 2 Corinthiens 2:17; ἐκ τ. ἀληθείας, Jean 18:37, 1 Jean 3:19; ὁ ἐκ πίστεως, Romains 3:26 4:16; οἱ (ὄντες) ἐκ περιτομῆς, Actes 11:2, Romains 4:12, Galates 2:12, Colossiens 4:11; πίνειν ἐκ, Matthieu 26:29, Marc 14:25, Jean 4:13, al.; θερίζειν, Galates 6:8; μετέχειν ἐκ (= partit. genitive), 1 Corinthiens 10:13; with inf., ἐκ τοῦ ἔχειν, 2 Corinthiens 8:11. 
__5. Of material: Matthieu 27:29, Jean 2:15 19:2, Romains 9:21, 1 Corinthiens 11:12, Apocalypse 18:12, al.; allied to which is its use of price (= cl. genitive): Matthieu 27:7, cf. ib. 20:2, Actes 1:18. 
__IV. By attraction = ἐν (cl.): τὰ ἐκ τ. οἰκιας, Matthieu 24:17; τ. ἐξ αὐτοῦ δύναμιν, Marc 5:30 (see Field, in l.); ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, Luc 11:13. 
__V. Adverbial phrases: ἐξ ἀνάγκης, 2 Corinthiens 9:7, Hébreux 7:12; ἐξ ἰσότητος, 2 Corinthiens 8:13; ἐκ μέρους, 1 Corinthiens 12:27 13:9-12; ἐκ μέτρου, Jean 3:34; ἐκ συμφώνου, 1 Corinthiens 7:5. 
__VI. in composition, ἐκ signifies, 
__1. procession, removal: ἐκβαίνω, ἐκβάλλω. 
__2. Opening out, unfolding: ἐκτείνω; metaphorically, ἐξαγγάλλω. 
__3. Origin: ἔκγονος. 
__4. Completeness: ἐξαπορέω (see M, Pr., 237), ἐκπληρόω, ἐκτελέω.

G1538.def:
1. every, every one, each, each one , Lat. quisque, (Homer), etc.; the singular is often joined with a pl. Verb, ἔβαν οἴκονδε ἕκαστος they went home every one of them , (Iliad by Homer); ἕκαστος ἐπίστασθε (Xenophon Historicus):—;the singular is also put in apposition with a pl. Noun, Τρῶας ἕκαστον ὑπήλυθε τρόμος (for Τρώων ἕκαστον)) fear seized them every one , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. in plural all and each one , (Homer) 
3. more definitely, εἷς ἕκαστος, Lat. unusquisque, every single one, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; καθ᾽ ἕκαστον singly, by itself , Lat. singulatim, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
4. ὡς ἕκαστοι each by himself , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G1539.def:
ἑκάστοτε 
adv., 
each time, always: 2 Pierre 1:15.†

G1540.def:
ἑκατόν, οἱ, αἱ, τά
indecl., 
a hundred: Matthieu 13:8, 23 Luc 15:4, al.; κατὰ ἑ, Marc 6:40; εἰς, ἐν ἑ., Marc 4:8, 20

G1541.def:
ἑκατονταετής (Rec. έτης), -ές 
(ἑκατόν, ἔτης) [in LXX for שָׁנֶה מֵאָה בֵּן, Genèse 17:17 * ;] 
a hundred years old: Romains 4:19.†

G1542.def: a hundred times as much or many , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G1543.def:
ἑκατοντάρχης (-άρχος, Matthieu 8:5, 8 27:54, Luc 7:2, Actes 22:25 28:16; cf. M, Pr., 48); -ου 
(ἑκατόν, ἄρχω,), [in LXX for מֵאָה שַׂר ;] 
a centurion: Matthieu 8:13, Luc 7:6 23:47, Actes 10:1, 22 21:32 22:26 23:17, 23 24:23 27:1, 6 27:11, 31 27:43 (cf. κεντυρίως).†

G1544.def:
ἐκ-βάλλω 
[in LXX chiefly for גָּרַשׁ pi., also for שָׁלַךְ hi., יָצָא hi., יָרַשׁ hi., etc. ;] 
__1. to drive, cast or send out, to expel: with accusative of thing(s), mid. (σῖτον), before εἰς, Actes 27:38; pass., Matthieu 15:17; with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 21:12, Marc 11:15, al.; δαιμόνια, Matthieu 7:22, Marc 1:34, al.; id. before ἐκ, Marc 7:26; παρά, Marc 16:9; ἐν, Marc 3:22; (ἐν) τ. ὀνόματι, Matthieu 7:22, Marc 9:38; λόγῳ, Matthieu 8:16; before ἔξω, Jean 6:37; id. with genitive, Marc 12:8, al.; of expulsion from home, Galates 4:30; from the Church, III Jn 10. 
__2. In LXX and NT (like Heb. יָצָא and Aram. הַנְפֵּק), to command or cause to depart: Matthieu 9:38, Marc 1:12 (see Swete, in l.), ib. Marc 1:43 5:40, Luc 10:2, Jacques 2:25; τ. κρίσιν εἰς νῖκος (to cause to proceed to its goal), Matthieu 12:20 (LXX). 
__3. to reject (cl.): τ. ὄνομα ὑμῶς ὡς πονηρόν (cf. Deutéronome 25:14), Luc 6:22; to leave out, Apocalypse 11:2. 
__4. to take, draw or pluck out; 
__(a) with violence: Matthieu 7:5, Marc 9:47, Luc 6:42; 
__(b) to bring forth or out of: Matthieu 12:35, Luc 10:35.

G1545.def:
ἔκ-βασις, -εως, ἡ
(ἐκβαίνω), [in LXX: Wis.2:17 8:8 11:14 * ;] 
__1. a way out (Hom., Xen.): 1 Corinthiens 10:13. 
__2. the issue (Menand.) Hébreux 13:7.†

G1546.def:
ἐκ-βολή, -ῆς
(ἐκβάλλω), [in LXX: Exode 11:1 (גָּרַשׁ), Josué 1:5 (ἐκβολὴν ποιεῖσθαι, טול hi.), Eze.47:8 (יָצָא)* ;] 
__1. a throwing out. 
__2. a jettison, a throwing overboard of cargo: Actes 27:18 (cf. Jos, l.with; and see Field, Notes, 144 f.).†

G1549.def:
ἔκ-γονος, -ον
(ἐκγίγνομαι, to be born of), [in LXX for פְּרִי (neut.), בֵּן, etc. ;] 
__1. with genitive, born of. 
__2. As subst., ὁ, ἡ ἔ., a child, son or daughter; in pl., descendants: τέκνα ἢ ἔ., children or grand-children, 1 Timothée 5:4.†

G1550.def:
εκ-δαπανάω, -ῶ 
strengthened form of δαπανάω, to spend wholly; pass., with reflexive force, to spend oneself wholly: before ὑπέρ, 2 Corinthiens 12:15.†

G1551.def:
ἐκ-δέχομαι 
[in LXX for עֶרֶב, קָבַץ, etc. ;] 
__1. to take or receive from (Hom., Hdt., a1.). 
__2. (Rare in cl.), to expect, await: with accusative of thing(s), Jean 5:3, Hébreux 11:10, Jacques 5:7; with accusative of person(s), Actes 17:16, 1 Corinthiens 11:33 16:11; before ἕως, Hébreux 10:13 (Cremer, 687).†

G1552.def:
ἔκ-δηλος, -ον
(δῆλος), [in LXX: 3Ma.3:19 3Mac 6:5 * ;] 
strengthened form of δῆλος, which see, quite clear, evident: 2 Timothée 3:9.†

G1554.def:
ἐκ-δίδωμι 
[in LXX for נָתַן, etc. ;] 
__1. to surrender, give up, give out. 
__2. to let out for hire (Hdt.); mid. (as frequently in π.; see MM, Exp., xii); to let out to one's advantage, Matthieu 21:33, 41, Marc 12:1, Luc 20:9.†

G1555.def:
ἐκ-δι-ηγέομαι, -οῦμαι depon., 
[in LXX chiefly for סָפַר, pi. ;] 
to tell in detail, relate, declare: Actes 13:41 (LXX) Actes 15:3.†

G1556.def:
ἐκδικέω, -ῶ
(ἔκδικος), [in LXX for פָּקַד, נָקַם, שָׁפַט, etc. ;] 
__1. to vindicate: with accusative of person(s), Luc 18:3, 5. 
__2. to avenge: with accusative of person(s), ἑαυτούς, Romains 12:19; with accusative of thing(s), παρακοήν, 2 Corinthiens 10:6; αἷμα, Apocalypse 6:10 19:2 (Cremer, 203; for exx. from π. in both senses, see MM, Exp., xii).†

G1557.def:
ἐκ-δίκησις, -εως, ἡ
(ἐκδικέω), [in LXX chiefly for נָקָם ;] 
vengeance, vindication: Luc 21:22, Romains 12:19 (see MM, Exp., xii), Hébreux 10:30 (LXX), 2 Corinthiens 7:11; of the injured person, with genitive, Luc 18:7-8; with dative, Actes 7:24; of the offender, with genitive obj., 1 Pierre 2:14; with dative, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:8 (cf. Sir.12:6).†

G1558.def:
ἔκδικος, -ον
(δίκη), [in LXX: Wis.12:12, Sir.30:6, 4Ma.15:29 * ;] 
__1. without law, unjust. 
__2. exacting penalty from; as subst., an avenger: Romains 13:4; before περί, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:6 (in π., a legal representative; Milligan, Th., l.with).†

G1559.def:
ἐκ-διώκω 
[in LXX for בָּרַח hi., צָמַת, הָדַף, etc. ;] 
to chase away, drive out: 1 Thessaloniciens 2:15 (cf. Deutéronome 6:19, Joël 2:20).†

G1560.def:
ἔκ-δοτος, -ον
(ἐκδίδωμι), [in LXX: Da TH Bel 1:22 * ;] 
given up, delivered over: Actes 2:23 (for construction, see Field, Notes, 111 f.).†

G1562.def:
ἐκ-δύω 
[in LXX chiefly for פָּשַׁט ;] 
to take of, strip of, strip: with accusative of person(s) (sc. clothing), Matthieu 27:28; with accusative of person(s) and of thing(s), Matthieu 27:31, Marc 15:20, Luc 10:30; mid., to put off: figuratively, of the body, 2 Corinthiens 5:4.†

G1563.def:
ἐκεῖ 
adv., [in LXX chiefly for שָׁם ;] 
__1. properly, of place, there: Matthieu 2:13 5:24, al.; οἱ ἐ., Matthieu 26:71; οὗ . . . ἐ., Matthieu 6:21 18:20 24:28, Marc 6:10, Luc 12:34; pleonastic, ὅπου . . . ἐ. (= שָׁם אֲשֶׁר, Deutéronome 4:5, al.), Apocalypse 12:6, 14 (cf. Bl., § 50, 4). 
__2. As often in cl. (Hdt., Thuc., al.), with verbs of motion, for ἐκεῖσε, thither: Matthieu 2:22 17:20 24:28 26:36, Marc 6:33, Luc 12:18 17:37 21:2, Jean 11:8 18:2-3, Romains 15:24

G1564.def:
ἐκεῖθεν 
adv., [in LXX chiefly for שָׁם ;] 
__1. of place, thence: Matthieu 4:21, Marc 6:1, al. 
__2. Of time, thereafter (see: κἀκεῖθεν).

G1565.def:
ἐκεῖνος, -η, -ο 
(ἐκεῖ), [in LXX chiefly for הַהוּא ,הוּא, and cogn. forms ;] 
demonstr. pron., 
that person or thing (ille), implying remoteness as compared with οὗτος (hic); 
__1. absol., emphatic he, she, it: opposite to οὗτος, Luc 18:14, Jacques 4:15; ἡμεῖς, Hébreux 12:25; ὑμεῖς, Marc 4:11; ἄλλοι, Jean 9:9; ἐγώ, Jean 3:30; to persons named, Mk 16:[10, 13, 20], Jean 2:21; of one (absent) who is not named, contemptuously (Abbott, JG, §§2385, 2732), Jean 7:11 9:28; with respect, of Christ, 1Jo.2:6 3:3, al.; referring to a preceding noun, Mrk.16:[10], Jean 7:45; resumption of a participial subject, Jean 1:33 9:37 10:1, Romains 14:14, al. (on its reference in Jean 19:35, see Westc, in l.; Moffatt, Intr., 568; Sanday, Fourth Gospel, 77ff.). 
__2. As adj., joined, like οὗτος, to a noun with the article: Matthieu 7:25, Marc 3:24, Jean 18:15, al.; esp. of time, past or future: ἐν τ. ἡμέραις ἐ., Matthieu 3:1, Marc 1:9, Actes 2:18" (LXX), al.; ἐν ἐ. τ. ἡμέρᾳ, esp of the Parousia, Matthieu 7:22, Luc 6:23, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:10, 2 Timothée 1:12; adverbially, ἐκεινής (sc. ὁδοῦ) = cl. ἐκεινῇ (Bl., §36, 13), that way, Luc 19:4.

G1566.def:
ἐκεῖσε 
adv., [in LXX: Job 39:29 שָׁם * ;] 
thither: Actes 21:3; constr. pregn. (MM, Exp., xii; Field, Notes, 134), τοὺς ἐ. ὄντας, Actes 22:5.†

G1567.def:
ἐκ-ζητέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX chiefly for דָּרַשׁ, also for נָצַר, בָּקַשׁ, etc. ;] 
__1. to seek out or after, search for: with accusative of person(s) (1Ma.9:26); figuratively, τ. κύριον, θεόν (cf. Psaumes 14:2, Amos 5:4, al.), Actes 15:17, Romains 3:11, Hébreux 11:6; εὐλογίαν, Hébreux 12:17; ἐξεζήτησαν κ. ἐξηραύνησαν (as in 1Ma.9:26), sought and searched out: 1 Pierre 1:10. 
__2. As in 2 Rois 4:11, Eze.3:18, 20 al. (דָּרַשׁ), to demand, require: Luc 11:50-51 †

G1568.def:
ἐκ-θαμβέω, -ῶ
(ἔκθαμβος), [in LXX: Sir.30:9 * ;] 
__1. to be amazed. 
__2. to amaze, terrify (Sir.30:9). Pass., to be amazed, terrified: Marc 9:15 14:33 16:5-6.†

G1569.def:
ἔκ-θαμβος, -ον
(θάμβος), [in LXX: Wis.10:19, Da TH Daniel 7:7 (dreadful, terrible: אֵמְתָּנִי) * ;] 
amazed (cf. Polyb., xx, 10, 9): Actes 3:11.†

G1570.def:
ἔκ-θετος, -ον
(ἐκτίθημι), [in Al.: Eze.42:3 * ;] 
cast out: ποιεῖν ἔ. = ἐκτιθέναι, Actes 7:19.†

G1571.def:
ἐκ-καθαίρω 
[in LXX for בָּעַר, etc. ;] 
__1. to cleanse thoroughly, cleanse out: with accusative, ἑαυτόν, 2 Timothée 2:21; of the impurity removed, ζυμήν, 1 Corinthiens 5:7.†

G1572.def:
ἐκ-καίω 
[in LXX chiefly for בָּעַר ;] 
__1. to burn up. 
__2. to kindle. Pass., to burn: metaphorically, of the passions (cf. Sir.16:6, Job 3:17), Romains 1:27.†

G1573.def:
ἐκκακέω, -ῶ, see: ἐνκακέω.
ἐν-κακέω, -ῶ (LTr., ἐγκ-; Rec. ἐκκ-; cf. WH, Notes, 157 f.; κακός, cowardly), 
[in Sm.: Genèse 27:46, Nombres 21:5, Proverbes 3:11, Ésaïe 7:16 *;] 
to lose heart : Luc 18:1, 2 Corinthiens 4:1,16, Galates 6:9, Éphésiens 3:13, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:13 (Cremer, 330).†

G1574.def:
ἐκ-κεντέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX chiefly for דָּקַר ;] 
__1. to prick out, put out (Arist.). 
__2. to pierce (Polyb., LXX): with accusative of person(s), Jean 19:37 (LXX), Apocalypse 1:7.†

G1575.def:
ἐκ-κλάω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Lévitique 1:17 (שָׁסַע pi.)* ;] 
to break off: pass., Romains 11:17-20.†

G1576.def:
ἐκ-κλείω 
[in LXX: ἐ. κρίσιν, for נָטָה hi., Exode 23:2 (also as seel., Job 34:20, Psaumes 67:1-7 (Psaumes 68:30) * ;] 
to shut out: Galates 4:17. Pass., Romains 3:27.†

G1578.def:
ἐκ-κλίνω 
[in LXX for נָטָה, סוּר, etc. ;] 
intrans., to turn aside, turn away: metaphorically, from the right path, absol., Romains 3:12 (LXX); from evil, absol., 1 Pierre 3:11; before ἀπό, with genitive of person(s), Romains 16:17.†

G1579.def: to swim out of , with genitive, (Euripides) (ML)

G1580.def:
ἐκ-κομίζω 
to carry out: as freq., a corpse for burial, Luc 7:12.†

G1581.def:
ἐκ-κόπτω, 
[in LXX for כָּרַת, etc. ;] 
to cut out, cut off, cut down: of a hand, foot, Matthieu 5:30 18:8; a tree, Matthieu 3:10 7:19 Luc 3:9 13:7, 9; figuratively, of a branch, Romains 11:22; before ἐκ, Romains 11:24; metaphorically, τ. ἀφορμήν (cf. Job 19:10 ἐλπίδα), 2 Corinthiens 11:12.†

G1582.def:
ἐκ-κρέμαννυμι, 
[in LXX for קָשַׁר, Genèse 44:30 * ;] 
to hang from or upon; mid., ἐκκρέμαμαι: figuratively, ἐξεκρέματο αὐτοῦ άκούων (Rec.; WH read ἐξεκρέμετο, which implies a Pres. ἐκκρέμομαι, otherwise unknown; cf. Veitch, see word κρέμαμαι), Luc 19:48.†

G1583.def:
ἐκ-λαλέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Jdth.11:9 * ;] 
to speak out, divulge: Actes 23:22.†

G1584.def:
ἐκ-λάμπω 
[in LXX for אוֹר hi., etc. ;] 
to shine forth: Matthieu 13:43.†

G1585.def:
ἐκ-λανθάνω 
[in Sm.: Psaumes 13:2 * ;] 
to escape notice utterly; mid., to forget utterly: Hébreux 12:5.†

G1586.def:
ἐκ-λέγω 
[in LXX chiefly for בָּחַר ;] 
to pick out, choose. In NT always mid. (exc. Luc 9:35, ἐκλελεγμένος, WH, ἀγαπητός, R, mg.), to pick out for oneself, choose (cf. M, Pr., 157 f.): with accusative of thing(s), Luc 10:42 14:7; with accusative of person(s), Actes 6:5 15:22, 25; of Christ (see supr.), Luc 9:35; of Christ's choice of disciples, Luc 6:13, Jean 6:70 13:18 15:16, 19 Actes 1:2; of the Divine choice: of persons, Marc 13:20, Actes 1:24 13:17 15:7, Éphésiens 1:4, Jacques 2:5; of things, 1 Corinthiens 1:27-28 (Cremer, 402, 773).†

G1587.def:
ἐκ-λείπω 
[in LXX for כָּלָה, כָּרַת ni., תָּמַם, etc., 47 different words in all ;] 
__1. trans., to leave out, pass over. 
__2. Intrans., to leave off, cease, fail: μαμωνᾶς, Luc 16:9; πίστις, Luc 22:32; ἔτη, Hébreux 1:12 (LXX); of the sun in an eclipse, Luc 23:45.†

G1589.def:
ἐκλογή, ῆς ἡ
(ἐκλέγω), [in Aq.: Ésaïe 22:7; Sm., Th.: Ésaïe 37:24 * ;] 
a choice, selection; in NT, always of the Divine choice (EV, election): σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς, genitive qual., a chosen vessel; κατ ἐ., Romains 9:11 11:5, 28; with genitive of person(s), 1 Thessaloniciens 1:4, 2 Pierre 1:10; by meton., ἡ ἐ. = οἱ ἐκλεκτοί, Romains 11:7.†

G1590.def:
ἐκ-λύω 
[in LXX for רָפָה, etc. ;] 
__1. to loose, release. 
__2. to unloose, as a bow-string, to relax, enfeeble; pass., to be faint, grow weary: Matthieu 15:32, Marc 8:3; of mental weariness, Galates 6:9, Hébreux 12:3, 5" (LXX) .†

G1591.def:
ἐκ-μάσσω 
[in LXX: Sir.12:11, Ep. Jérémie 13:1-27 24:1-10 * ;] 
to wipe off: with accusative, Luc 7:38, 44, Jean 11:2 12:3 13:5.†

G1592.def:
ἐκ-μυκτηρίζω 
[in LXX: Psaumes 2:4 22:7 35:16 (לָעַג), I Esther 1:51 A* ;] 
to hold up the nose in derision at, scoff at: with accusative, Luc 16:14 23:35.†

G1593.def:
ἐκ-νεύω 
[in LXX: Juges 4:18 (סוּר) Juges 18:26, 4Ki.2:24 23:16 (פָּנָה), Michée 6:14 (סוּג hi.), 3Ma.3:22 * ;] 
__1. to bend the head aside (Xen.). 
__2. 
__(a) to shun, avoid (Diod.); 
__(b) to withdraw: Jean 5:13†

G1594.def:
ἐκ-νήφω 
[in LXX: Genèse 9:24, Habacuc 2:7 (יָקַץ), Joël 1:5, Habacuc 2:19 (יָקַץ hi.), 1 Rois 25:37 (יָצָא), Sir.31:2 * ;] 
to become sober after drunkenness: metaphorically, of sobriety of mind, 1 Corinthiens 15:34.†

G1595.def:
ἐκούσιος, -ον
(έκών), [in LXX chiefly for נְדָבָה, as Nombres 15:3 (κατ᾽ ἑ) ;] 
usually of actions, voluntary: κατὰ ἑ., of free will (Lft., in l), Phm 14.†

G1596.def:
ἑκουσίως 
adv., [in LXX: Psaumes 54:6 (נְדָבָה) 2Ma.14:3, al. ;] 
voluntarily, willingly: Hébreux 10:26, 1 Pierre 5:2.†

G1597.def:
ἔκ-παλαι 
adv. (of a class of compound adverbs common in late Gk.; see Mayor on 2 Pe, l.with), 
for a long time, from of old: 2 Pierre 2:3 3:5.†

G1598.def:
ἐκ-πειράζω 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 6:16 8:2, 16 Psaumes 78:18 (נָסָה pi.) * ;] 
= cl. ἐκπειράομαι, 
to put to the proof or test, make trial of, tempt: with accusative, of God, Matthieu 4:7 (LXX), Luc 4:12 (ib.), 1 Corinthiens 10:9; of Christ, Luc 10:25 (Cremer, 497).†

G1599.def:
ἐκ-πέμπω 
[in LXX for שָׁלַח ;] 
to send forth: Actes 13:4 17:10.†
